messages.subject: new application layout functions
parts:
Hello all,

We've recently added some capabilities to the development version of Shiny aimed at improving core application layout. Specifically there are new features that:

(1) Make it easier to create custom page layouts using the Bootstrap grid system

(2) Provide navigation containers for creating larger applications (Navbars and Navlists)

There's a write-up of the new features here: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Shiny-Application-Layout-Guide

If you want to try out the new features you should install Shiny from Github as follows:

devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio")

Let us know whether everything works as expected and what improvements you think would make sense. Thanks!

-- The Shiny team

Sure. Here's an example of an application that use a navbar to divide the application into two top-level panels. The first of them has a sidebar with main panel layout and the second uses a tabset:

shinyUI(navbarPage("Application Title",
  
  tabPanel("Component 1",
    sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel("Sidebar"),
      mainPanel("Main")
    )
  ),    
    
  tabPanel("Component 2",
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Tab 1"),
      tabPanel("Tab 2"),
      tabPanel("Tab 3")
    )
  )  
))

messages.subject: Re: new application layout functions
parts: Currently, as I see it,  on running it defaults to a blank page - other than header and footer info.

By default the navbarPage should select the first tabPanel. You could name this "Home" if you wanted it to be a starter page for the whole application. In the example you don't see this since the first panel is empty but if you execute this code you'll see the content in the first panel at startup:

shinyUI(navbarPage("App Title",
  tabPanel("Plot", 
    h3("Plot Panel")
  ),
  tabPanel("Summary"),
  tabPanel("Table")
))

In fact b) would be better as I would like to be able to refer to a specific tabPanel, say panel1, and then only
call the relevant code within server.R. e.g source('panel1_code.R', local=TRUE)
You get this behavior automatically insofar as code with outputs that only appear on a given tabPanel will not be executed until the tabPanel is visible.
